trace.sourceFact: One CasesBegin object is created, pushed by EqnArray, pushed again by NumCases, and followed by the returned EqnArray item. The two logical CasesBegin entries alias one object.

Each closing SpreadLines handler removes the actual top directly, calls toMml without Clear, applies spacing, and pushes the MML. Pop bypasses matching-End checks and retains open-item env. Final MML appends into the exposed item, so shared node aliases and recipients require measurement.

A first matching End with truthy Cases end flips the shared flag and returns [[],true]; Stack.Push then removes one logical entry and recursively pushes zero items. NumCases reads stack.Top after that operation rather than retaining its incoming begin as recipient.

Last is _nodes[0] (oldest), First is the newest node. NumCases copies then-current Top.Last before obtaining left from that same then-current Top. Item-local properties are separate from copied lexical env. Do not substitute the original Cases left string or the newest node for a lower recipient.

The selected node is passed to left-decoration operations with left+helper; afterward NumCases pushes a second matching End. Non-table, empty, table, wrapper, and missing-property behavior must be captured as complete original APIs rather than assigned source-only expectations.

trace.sourceHypothesis: The authored prefixes/wrappers attempt to exercise different public lower recipients. Earlier reductions, including Fn/position reductions before Cases, can alter the actual item lifetime. The second direct Pop and subsequent matching-End transition may expose a lower item with its own node stack and close reductions. Family names and intended recipients are not observed parser-state or outcome claims.

content.scope: Frozen default-profile built-in MoveLeftRight Position constructor/checkItem/Stack.Push lifetime; no claim excluding other own-left recipients.

sourceFacts.fact: MoveLeftRight calls create('position') with no node arguments, then sets move='horizontal' and left/right mspace properties. BaseItem's empty rest-node array becomes MmlStack._nodes. The mspace values are properties, not initial stored nodes.

Position has no isOpen override. Nonfinal input delegated to BaseItem does not append nodes. On final MML, horizontal Position returns [mml(left), item, mml(right)], true before BaseItem's final-node append branch can run.

Stack.Push removes the current Position when checkItem returns that replacement list, then recursively replays it into the exposed lower item. Final MML therefore removes horizontal Position instead of leaving it alive with a stored oldest node.
An earlier public P+Q prefix is stored on the lower item before Position is created. Pushing Position copies/attaches lexical env but does not copy the lower item's node stack into Position.

The Cases first-End empty replacement pops an alias and pushes zero nodes. If that transition exposes an intact built-in horizontal Position, its Last is still absent (_nodes[0]). NumCases invokes copyNode(Last) before getProperty('left'); this source ordering precedes horizontal property's string coercion.

content.boundedConclusion: An intact built-in horizontal Position exposed by this Cases transition cannot have a nonempty oldest stored Last through its ordinary constructor/checkItem/Push transitions. Its own left property exists, but no stored node is accumulated while the item remains live. This horizontal case alone does not justify or rule out generic own-property/value-coercion modeling for other recipient types.

NumCases reads and stores its mandatory left argument at102–103 before EqnArray. EqnArray pushes the Cases begin at1491 before checkEqnEnv1492–1494 and before any Cases body parse.

Subsup accepts only item kinds open or left at236–238, not every item with isOpen. Cases begin kind is cases-begin. This nonfinal kind enters BaseItem's success branch and the Subsup missing-open throw at261–264; this source transition precedes EqnArray's nesting check and the authored body token.

sourceTrace.sourceFact: The authored horizontal command is followed by P. Frozen variable() immediately pushes P as a node; Stack.Push wraps it as final mml. Horizontal Position therefore takes its final-node replacement path at P rather than retaining P as a stored node.

Prime obtains its base from then-current Top through Prev and installs a Prime item. When EqnArray later pushes CasesBegin, Prime.checkItem returns its settled node together with the incoming item for replay. The source does not justify assuming horizontal Position is still live at this settlement, or assuming the authored P remains the selected Prime base after horizontal replacement.
